title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple lost approximately $800,000 to cryptocurrency scammers who used AI-generated imagery to create a fake website. The website displayed false account balances, making it appear that investments were growing when they were not. The scam began with a WhatsApp message from a stranger and progressed through a legitimate mobile trading app, where the attackers established trust by permitting small trades and withdrawals before requesting larger sums.

The failure was in the visual authentication layer. The victims could see a website showing their supposed account balances, but that website was fabricated using AI-generated content. Nothing in the reporting establishes whether the legitimate trading app itself was compromised, or whether the scammers directed victims to the fake site through social engineering. A manual verification step, such as a phone call from the app provider or an in-person visit to confirm the investment, would likely have exposed the deception.

It is not established what safeguards the legitimate trading app had in place, or whether regulatory authorities have taken action against the app provider for being the vector through which victims were initially contacted.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. Jerry Dunaway was encouraged to invest in cryptocurrency through a mobile trading app, and the scammers built his trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts. Over time, the investments grew larger, but when Dunaway tried to withdraw a significant sum, he discovered the money was gone. Police revealed that while the trading app was legitimate, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false account balances on Dunaway's screen.

The couple is now working with Gwinnett County police but faces a difficult recovery process, as authorities say victims in these cases rarely recover their stolen funds. Despite their financial devastation and embarrassment, the Dunaways decided to speak publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by these scammers. Their children have created a GoFundMe page to help their parents with daily expenses as they work to rebuild their lives.
